original_question: Is it consistent that the dominating number d is singular and nevertheless the strong polarized relation \( inom{d}{\omega} 	o  inom{d}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.7: “Is it consistent that \mathfrak{d} is a singular cardinal and \binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2?” ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already lands on the exact local target of the paper: it uses the right invariant (the dominating number \mathfrak{d}), the right extra hypothesis (that \mathfrak{d} be singular), and the right positive strong polarized relation with second coordinate \omega and 2 colors. In substance, it is essentially Problem 3.7 itself. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, explicitly define \mathfrak{d} as the classical dominating number on \omega^\omega, i.e. the least size of a family F\subseteq\omega^\omega such that every g\in\omega^\omega is eventually dominated by some f\in F.

Unpack the polarized notation via Definition 1.1: for every coloring c:\mathfrak{d}\times\omega\to 2 there must be A\subseteq\mathfrak{d} and B\subseteq\omega with |A|=\mathfrak{d} and |B|=\omega such that c\upharpoonright(A\times B) is constant. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
Make the ambient metamathematical quantifier explicit: the question is about relative consistency with ZFC (equivalently, whether there is a model of ZFC in which this happens).

Keep the scope tied to Section 3, i.e. the countable second coordinate \omega; do not broaden it to the later singular-cardinal problems of Section 4, which concern pairs like (\lambda^+,\lambda). ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

Do not add extra assumptions such as \mathfrak{d}<\mathfrak{c}, \mathfrak{u}<\mathfrak{d}, or \mathfrak{d}\leq\mathfrak{u}; those belong to neighboring Problems 3.8 and 3.9, not to Problem 3.7. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
refined_question: Is it consistent with ZFC that the dominating number \mathfrak{d}=\min\{ |F| : F\subseteq\omega^\omega\ \text{and}\ (\forall g\in\omega^\omega)(\exists f\in F)\, g\leq^* f\} is singular (that is, \operatorname{cf}(\mathfrak{d})<\mathfrak{d}) and nevertheless the strong polarized relation \binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 holds, meaning that for every coloring c:\mathfrak{d}\times\omega\to 2 there exist A\subseteq\mathfrak{d} and B\subseteq\omega with |A|=\mathfrak{d} and |B|=\omega such that c\upharpoonright(A\times B) is constant?
justification: The draft is aiming at exactly Section 3, Problem 3.7. The nearby discussion explains why this is the precise sharp formulation: the authors note that for every regular \kappa>\aleph_1 one can force \mathfrak{d}=\kappa together with \binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2, but that the Blass–Shelah model used there requires \mathfrak{d} to be regular; since \mathfrak{d} may nevertheless be singular, they isolate exactly the singular-\mathfrak{d} case as Problem 3.7. Definition 1.1 supplies the needed meaning of the strong polarized relation. The paper does not state an explicit equivalent reformulation of Problem 3.7, so none should be added. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
